sentences.text: We wanted to know whether the amount of sugar changes how fast yeast makes carbon dioxide.
Our hypothesis is that more sugar would make the balloon grow faster.
We mixed one packet of yeast with 100 mL of warm water in each of four bottles.
Each bottle got 0, 5, 10 or 20 grams of sugar, and we stretched a balloon over its neck.
Every five minutes for thirty minutes we measured around each balloon with a string and a ruler.
We kept the water warm the whole time.
After thirty minutes the balloon on the 20 gram bottle was a lot bigger than the others.
The bottle with no sugar did not change at all.
More sugar made the balloons grow faster, which proves our hypothesis.
This happens because yeast breaks down sugar for energy and gives off carbon dioxide as it does.
The temperature also matters because yeast is alive.
We only did each bottle once.
